what: Predict species occurrence with the geo model
title: Get started with birdnetR
text: BirdNET includes geographic model predicts species likely occur location week year. returns prediction object species names scores. BirdNET’s year 48 weeks: four per month, week 1 first week January week 48 last week December. week = NULL (default), model predicts whole year. year_round_aggregation decides weekly scores combined: "max" (default) "average". can use geo prediction species list acoustic model. Every name species_list must known acoustic model, take names acoustic model’s list. two models can name species differently, match names scientific name, common name rest. Use geo acoustic models version:
code: # Load the geo model geo_model <- birdnet_load(type = "geo")  # Predict species occurrence in Ithaca, NY in week 4 (the end of January) predictions <- birdnet_predict(geo_model, latitude = 42.5, longitude = -76.45, week = 4L)  # Convert to a data frame and sort by score df <- as.data.frame(predictions) head(df[order(-df$confidence), ])  # Example output: #>                           species_name confidence #>     Spinus tristis_American Goldfinch  0.9998151 #>        Junco hyemalis_Dark-eyed Junco  0.9997241 #>  Dryobates pubescens_Downy Woodpecker  0.9997090 #>        Zenaida macroura_Mourning Dove  0.9996312 predictions <- birdnet_predict(geo_model, latitude = 42.5, longitude = -76.45) geo_species <- as.data.frame(predictions)$species_name acoustic_species <- birdnet_list_species(model)  # Names are "<scientific name>_<common name>" scientific <- function(x) sub("_.*", "", x) common <- function(x) sub("^[^_]*_", "", x) keep <- scientific(acoustic_species) %in% scientific(geo_species) |   common(acoustic_species) %in% common(geo_species)  predictions <- birdnet_predict(model, audio_path, species_list = acoustic_species[keep])
